questions.question:
**Identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error.**

Whenever I went to cinemas, I bought myself popcorn and coke for a special treat.
questions.solution:
The erroneous part is: **for**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The context of the sentence tells us that the author always treated herself with popcorn and a coke whenever she went to the movies.
 
• The **preposition** 'for' after 'coke' is grammatically incorrect.
 
• The preposition 'as' is used for talking about somebody/something’s** job, role or function**.
 
• In this context, it is talking about the function of popcorn and coke which acts as a special treat for the author.
 
• Hence, 'for' should be replaced by 'as'.

Therefore, the correct answer is: *Whenever I went to cinemas, I bought myself popcorn and coke **as** a special treat.*

options.text: Mrs. Nair remarked that children ate the wrong foods.

Mrs. Nair remarked that children eat the wrong foods.
Mrs. remarked that children have been eating the wrong foods.

questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 2.**

The given sentence is in the **present continuous tense in the direct speech.**

When we convert from direct to indirect speech, the following changes take place.

 
• The **Reported verb comes at the beginning** of the sentence and the **tense remains unchanged.**
 
• Determiner **'that'** is added and inverted commas are omitted.
 
• The tense of the **reporting speech changes from present continuous to past continuous tense => are eating => were eating.**

Following the rules of conversion, the sentence in the indirect speech will be: *Mrs. Nair remarked that children were eating the wrong foods.*

Other options are incorrect as they do not follow the rules of conversion.

**When we convert a sentence from direct to indirect speech, we make the following changes:**

 
• **Quotation marks** are **omitted** and the sentence** ends with a full stop**. 
 
• The **tense** of the **verb**, in the reported speech involving any **order, request and instruction** does** not undergo** any **change **during the conversion from direct to indirect mode. This is also true if the statement is a** universal truth.** 
 
• If the** reporting verb** is in the **present tense**, it does **not undergo** any **change**.
 
• We add the word** 'to' **before the verb if the verb is in **bare infinitive**.
 
• When the reporting or **principal verb** is in the **present tense**, all present tenses of the direct are **changed** into the corresponding** past tenses.**
 
• Words expressing **nearness in time or place** are generally converted into words expressing** distance**.

 For eg.** now** becomes **then**,** today** becomes **that day**, **yesterday** becomes **the previous day**, **this** becomes** that,** etc.
 
• In reporting **commands and requests**, the** verb expressing command or request **is **added** and the** imperative **is changed into the** infinitive.**
